reply_text:
*I’d fix the equal-split remainder bug before merging.* Reviewed `split-bill` against `main`; no code changed.

*CRITICAL*
• *`bill/split.py:4–5` — Remainder cents disappear.* `split_bill(1000, 3)` returns `[333, 333, 333]`, totaling 999; `split_bill(2, 3)` loses the entire bill.
  *Fix:* Use `divmod(total_cents, n)` and add one cent to each of the first remainder shares. Add tests for both examples—`tests/test_split.py` currently tests only exact divisions.

*INFORMATIONAL*
• *`bill/weighted.py:5–6` — Zero-weight people can receive leftover charges.* `weighted_split(1, [0, 1, 1])` returns `[1, 0, 0]`: the person with no weight pays everything.
  *Fix:* Either reject zero weights explicitly or distribute leftovers only among positive-weight participants.

• *`bill/weighted.py:2–6` — Empty/all-zero weights aren’t validated.* `weighted_split(100, [])` raises `IndexError`; `[0, 0]` raises `ZeroDivisionError`.
  *Fix:* Validate a nonempty weight list with a positive sum and reject invalid inputs with `ValueError`.

*Tip rounding needs a policy decision:* `bill/tip.py:2` uses Python’s ties-to-even rounding: a 0.5¢ tip becomes 0¢, while 1.5¢ becomes 2¢. That isn’t necessarily wrong, but if you intend half-cents always to round up, it needs changing and explicit tests.

All 5 existing tests pass; none tests tip rounding.
